t: The Kingdom of Poland of 1815 had one of the most liberal constitutions of 19th-century Europe, but the Russian emperors as its kings disregarded the limits on their power.
After the November Uprising of 1830–1831 and the January Uprising of 1863 its autonomy was dismantled and the land was ruled directly as part of the Russian Empire, officially called Vistula Land.
Congress Poland became the most industrialised region of the Russian Empire, with the textile centre of Łódź and Warsaw the empire's third-largest city.
dyk: In January 1831 the Sejm deposed Nicholas I as King of Poland, answering his repeated curtailing of its constitutional rights; he sent Russian troops into the country.
ev: The Congress of Vienna creates the Kingdom of Poland from most of the Duchy of Warsaw, ruled by Tsar Alexander I
Alexander I abolishes freedom of the press and introduces preventive censorship
The Sejm deposes Nicholas I, and the November Uprising is defeated after an 11-month campaign
The Organic Statute repeals the constitution and abolishes the army and the Sejm
The January Uprising breaks out and is crushed within two years
The Russian administration enfranchises the peasants, giving them ownership of their land
A reform divides the land into 10 governorates, and the name Vistula Land comes into official use
The Russian army retreats and the Central Powers occupy the kingdom

f.founder: The Congress of Vienna, with Tsar Alexander I as King of Poland; Adam Jerzy Czartoryski worked for its creation
f.successor: Government General of Warsaw, then the Kingdom of Poland of 1916 under the Central Powers
